A_CORE_SEMANTIC_TOOLS.definition: Every production MCP semantic tool registered in server.py that returns semantic facts about code. Pure maintenance tools (check_dependencies, check_ollama, configure_llm, get_active_build, get_environment_status, get_project_info, list_projects, list_variants, reindex_file, reset_index) are EXCLUDED — they return health/config/mutation status, not code-symbol semantic facts.

tools.name: get_vector_table
tools.note: registered directly without v2_authority_route; reads legacy vector table — NOT migrated to v2

tools.name: compare_variants
tools.note: SPECIALIZED_OPTIONAL (requires multi-variant index) — NOT migrated to v2 (server.py:1334)

tools.name: group_equivalent_variants
tools.note: SPECIALIZED_OPTIONAL (requires multi-variant index) — NOT migrated to v2 (server.py:1334)

excluded_maintenance_tools.name: check_dependencies
excluded_maintenance_tools.reason: dependency audit, not code semantic facts

excluded_maintenance_tools.name: get_active_build
excluded_maintenance_tools.reason: index health/status (canonical health-check gate); incidentally returns build-level defines/memory/entry_point but primary purpose is health

excluded_maintenance_tools.name: list_variants
excluded_maintenance_tools.reason: variant list (build identity, not code-symbol facts)

This is a naming inconsistency in the shadow schema documentation, NOT a count difference — there are still 12 distinct fact kinds emitted.

B_M6_FACT_KINDS.facts_py_note: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/facts.py defines the v2 StateFacts (Tier-T extraction: file_table/symbols/edges/conditions/positions/branch_states/root_edges/symbol_attrs) — NOT M6 fact kinds. M6 fact kinds are defined ONLY in m6_schema.py and emitted by m6_indexing.py. facts.py is the v2 store's own fact-row schema, a separate concept.

C_NORMAL_INDEX_ENTRYPOINTS.definition: User-facing CLI commands and the programmatic indexer entrypoint that normal users invoke to build/maintain the semantic index. Excludes config-only management commands (init-variants) and read-only commands (search, list, status, export, doctor).

entrypoints.name: fw-context index
entrypoints.note: primary full index build (parse + refs + embeddings + optional analyze)

entrypoints.name: fw-context index --build
entrypoints.note: force build + index variant of cmd_index (regenerates compile_commands.json then indexes)

entrypoints.name: fw-context init
entrypoints.note: project provisioning + dependency auto-fix + build-system detection + compile_commands.json generation (--skip-build off); prerequisite for indexing, does not itself write the semantic store

entrypoints.name: fw-context quickstart
entrypoints.note: alias for 'init --quick' — skips AI-tool registration but still provisions project + builds cc.json

entrypoints.name: fw-context analyze
entrypoints.note: re-runs LLM symbol analysis on the existing index (writes llm_analysis)

entrypoints.name: fw-context finetune
entrypoints.note: fine-tunes embedding model (regenerates embeddings used by semantic search)

entrypoints.name: fw-context watch
entrypoints.note: background file-watcher daemon that auto-reindexes on file change (spawns background reindex)

entrypoints.name: indexer/runner.py:run()
entrypoints.note: main programmatic indexing entrypoint called by cmd_index; parses TUs, extracts symbols/refs, writes v2 store (publish_one_shot + finalize_world), and legacy store when compat mode is on

excluded.name: fw-context search / list / status / export / doctor / db / cache
excluded.reason: read-only / diagnostic / config commands, do not build the index

D_NORMAL_LIFECYCLE_ENTRYPOINTS.evidence_worlds: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/worlds.py (World lifecycle: build → bind → finalize → GC)
D_NORMAL_LIFECYCLE_ENTRYPOINTS.definition: Public lifecycle entrypoints in gc.py and worlds.py that manage World and SemanticState lifecycle (creation, binding, finalization, GC, status transitions, claims).

entrypoints.name: analyze_gc
entrypoints.note: ANALYZE/dry-run: compute candidate Worlds/states for collection (no deletion)

entrypoints.name: apply_gc
entrypoints.note: APPLY: transactional deletion per approved reachability set

entrypoints.name: verify_gc
entrypoints.note: VERIFY: integrity checks after mutation

entrypoints.name: mark_world_failed
entrypoints.note: mark a World status='failed' (GC-eligible)

entrypoints.name: mark_world_retained
entrypoints.note: mark a World status='retained' (GC root)

entrypoints.name: mark_world_retired
entrypoints.note: mark a World status='retired' (GC-eligible)

entrypoints.name: build_world_context
entrypoints.note: construct the v2 World context for an indexing run

entrypoints.name: bind_tu
entrypoints.note: bind a TU (cert + facts) to a World

entrypoints.name: record_poison
entrypoints.note: record a poisoned TU binding (INV-6, never silently omitted)

entrypoints.name: finalize_world
entrypoints.note: DECISION Row-3 lifecycle: 'unfinalized' -> 'active' with checks (§28)

entrypoints.name: record_run_metrics
entrypoints.note: §40 persist per-run counters (auxiliary lifecycle-adjacent)

entrypoints.name: capture_extra_files
entrypoints.note: G10 capture non-TU files (assembly, linker scripts) into world_extra_files (auxiliary lifecycle-adjacent)

entrypoints.name: world_claim
entrypoints.note: World ownership claim with TTL (concurrency lifecycle)

D_NORMAL_LIFECYCLE_ENTRYPOINTS.strict_note: Excluding the 2 auxiliary entrypoints (record_run_metrics, capture_extra_files) gives 11 strict lifecycle-transition entrypoints. The 13-count includes them for completeness; the M7 program should audit all 13 since both are reachable from the normal indexing path.

E_NORMAL_FALLBACK_PATHS.definition: Distinct fallback/degradation code paths defined in the three specified files that normal production operation can take when a primary path is unavailable.

paths.name: lexical_fts5_fallback
paths.behavior: degrade to pure lexical FTS5 search with a warning; adds stale warnings

paths.name: shadow_dual_read_compat_fallback
paths.trigger: explicit legacy compat mode (_legacy_compat_on()=True) OR shadow_v2_enabled(); default OFF
paths.behavior: M5-2 migration scaffolding (compat-only); in v2-only mode (default) run_shadow just calls legacy_fn directly — never reached in normal production

paths.name: v2_unavailable_degrade
paths.trigger: no .fw-context dir or no index-v2.db exists
paths.behavior: v2 adapters return [] (list tools) or [warning] (semantic/smart) or None (single-symbol tools); the v2_authority_route then treats this as a v2 result (or, for None-returning tools, may raise -> equivalence-gated legacy fallback in authority.py)

paths.name: semantic_search_v2_like_fallback
paths.trigger: v2 has no embedding vectors (M3B degraded)
paths.behavior: perform LIKE-based search over symbol names/signatures with nominal _similarity scores; leading warning dict records the degradation

paths.name: smart_search_v2_like_partial_degradation
paths.trigger: v2 has no LLM backend (M3B degraded)
paths.behavior: perform a single LIKE pass (no multi-phase pipeline); leading warning dict with _partial=True records the degradation

E_NORMAL_FALLBACK_PATHS.related_production_read_fallback_note: The PRIMARY production read fallback — the v2-authority equivalence-gated legacy fallback — lives in src/fw_context_mcp/mcp/shared/authority.py:107-194 (route_authority), NOT in the three specified files. When a v2 adapter raises V2UnsupportedOperation / QueryViewResolutionError / any Exception, route_authority falls back to the legacy handler ONLY IF verify_legacy_equivalence confirms the same build (RISK B fix, D005); otherwise it returns the v2 error. This is the most critical normal production fallback path and is covered in authority_matrix.json (production_read_authority).

cross_check_vs_historical.investigation: The historical '29 tools' counts ONLY the v2_authority_route-wrapped (migrated) semantic tools. The actual code registers 32 core semantic tools: 29 v2-routed + 3 non-migrated (get_vector_table at server.py:1244, compare_variants at server.py:1335, group_equivalent_variants at server.py:1336). The +3 are explicitly marked SPECIALIZED_OPTIONAL / NOT migrated at server.py:1334 and registered directly without v2_authority_route. They ARE production semantic tools that return facts about code (interrupt vector table, variant comparison), so they belong in the CORE_SEMANTIC_TOOLS denominator. The M7 denominator should be 32 (all production semantic tools), with the 29 subset tracked separately as 'v2-migrated semantic tools'.
